findings.message: Explicit reuse evidence is inoperative end-to-end against the real API. server/projects.ts:547 normalizeEvents emits only type 'status_changed' or 'log' and hardcodes reused_from_attempt: null (and never 'result_reused', 'approval_requested', 'result_published' or 'artifact_published'), while src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx:184 derives the whole reuse panel from events with type === 'result_reused'. Consequently every node in candidate/production mode renders data-testid="reuse-none" ("No reuse evidence recorded"), including runs where one lane was retried and the sibling verification was reused - exactly this pipeline's failure drill (bundle failure_drill.verification_attempts: ui [1], adapter [1, 2]). The persisted export does contain non-guessed reuse evidence the adapter already reads: verification_packets attempt sets per lane, and tasks[].result preserving a successful sibling's pending writes (features/project-workflows/README.md: 'a task result can preserve a successful sibling's pending writes after another branch failed'), so this is not a case where the backend would have to infer reuse from status. The gap is not caught by verification because tests/project-workflows/projects.spec.ts:244-247 accepts either reuse-list or reuse-none in candidate phase. Fix requires either projecting explicit reuse into the v1 events (adapter) or sourcing the UI's reuse panel from evidence the API actually publishes; the candidate-phase assertion must then be tightened.
findings.requirement: Show statuses, attempts, explicit reuse evidence, changed files, actual checks, assumptions, logs and screenshots.

findings.message: Candidate-phase assertions are conditionally weakened beyond the reuse case. tests/project-workflows/projects.spec.ts:294-298 runs the failed-run evidence assertions (worker-error panel, 'Retrying is done through the workflow CLI') only when phase === 'worker', and line 306 asserts the approval message only in worker phase. In candidate mode the seeded RUN_FAILED does expose /results/adapter/1 with a gate-blocked result (status failed, error code VERIFICATION_BLOCKED), so the candidate phase could and should assert that the failure evidence panel renders from the real API; as written, candidate mode never verifies that failed/awaiting-approval evidence rendering works against the backend, only that the run/node status badges do.
findings.requirement: Do not skip tests in candidate mode, weaken assertions, or substitute a screenshot for testing interactions.

findings.message: Candidate recheck evidence is served but unreachable from the UI. server/projects.ts:591-609 assigns result_uri only for nodes in WORKER_OF (launch_ui/launch_adapter/verify_ui/verify_adapter), so the 'candidate' graph node always has result_uri null even when candidate-phase packets exist, and nothing in the client ever constructs /results/candidate_ui/N or /results/candidate_adapter/N (src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx only follows snapshot result_uri via scopedResultPath). The candidate node therefore displays data-testid="result-none" ("No result has been published for this node") while two hash-verified packets exist for it, which understates available evidence for the combined-candidate step. Documented as an open assumption, but it leaves a published API surface with no path to it in the viewer.
findings.requirement: All project-scoped read endpoints in the committed API contract: projects, definitions, paginated runs, pinned run detail, events, worker results and registered artifacts.

findings.message: Event status mapping is incomplete and silently degrades to pending. server/projects.ts:128 EVENT_STATUS covers only running/interactive/blocked/succeeded/passed/approved; persisted statuses such as 'failed', 'stopped', 'interrupted', 'awaiting_approval' and 'cancelled' map to null, so those events become type 'log' with status null and, in projectSnapshot, a node whose only evidence is such an event falls through to 'pending' (server/projects.ts:622-624). The current producer (workflow/pipeline.py) emits 'blocked' for failures so the live path is covered, but any producer-side status addition (automatic.py already emits 'interrupted', test paths emit 'stopped') is downgraded to an unattributed log line rather than surfaced, and a recorded failure that is not also a task error would render as 'not started'.
findings.requirement: Read actual persisted `run-state.json`, `plan.json`, events and verification packets under configured run roots.

findings.message: Run-list cost and blast radius. RunStore.listRuns (server/projects.ts:320) fully projects every run directory on every page request - parsing run-state.json and plan.json, reading and SHA-256-verifying every registered packet, and parsing all of events.jsonl - and the requested limit/cursor is applied only afterwards in projectRoutes.ts:126-129, so paging never bounds the work. Each read allocates Buffer.allocUnsafe(limit + 1) (16 MiB per export/plan/events/packet read, 32 MiB per artifact) regardless of file size. Separately, a single malformed run directory turns the entire workflow's run list into a 500 RUN_STORAGE_INVALID (invalidRun is thrown from inside the list loop), unlike legacy directories which are skipped with a warning; the same applies to a duplicated/non-increasing event sequence (server/projects.ts:512), which is plausible because workflow/pipeline.py derives sequences with only an in-process lock while the automatic supervisor runs controllers in successive processes. One corrupt run then hides every healthy run of that workflow.
findings.requirement: Do not execute Python, spawn processes or write run storage in response to a read request.

findings.message: Redaction is applied asymmetrically to worker results. projectWorkerResult (server/projects.ts:644-661) rewrites checks[].cwd to a run-relative path and redacts summary and gate reasons, but publishes checks[].command verbatim. Verifier-issued commands routinely embed absolute paths (this run's own packets record effective_commands with --output=/home/agentops/.local/state/...), so a producer that stored such a command in result.checks[].command would disclose a filesystem path through the results route, which the same function otherwise takes care to prevent.
findings.requirement: Map registered artifacts safely through packet registries: path confinement, symlink escape protection, hash checks, bounded reads, correct MIME types and safe errors without absolute path disclosure.

findings.message: Launch (kind worker) nodes expose the worker-phase verification result_uri (server/projects.ts:596-602), so once verification has run, the 'Launch UI worker' node renders a full verification WorkerResult - status, changed files, checks, artifacts - under a node whose success only means a native session launched, and the same result is shown again on verify_ui. The UI mitigates this with node-status-meaning text ('This is not workflow completion'), and it is listed as an open assumption, but it conflates launch evidence with verification evidence and duplicates one result across two graph nodes with different attempt numbers.
findings.requirement: A native worker turn ending is not workflow completion.
